scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode provides the active-step title, wrapping caption, wide-viewport ToC, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Header renders activeStep.title; Footer renders the full caption in an unrestricted paragraph, progress buttons, and previous/next buttons; Presentation includes Toc in browse mode.

evidence: usePresentationNav.toggleMode updates only mode state.

scene-kit.rationale: Swipe navigation does not reject predominantly vertical or multi-touch gestures.

scene-kit.rationale: Navigation exposes semantic current-state attributes and stable active styling hooks.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit exposes stable hooks across its structural output, controls, and entity primitives.
evidence: Presentation and Stage emit root, body, stage, viewport, canvas, and scene hooks. Header, Footer, Toc, and Attribution emit dedicated chrome and active-state hooks.
Box, Label, Frame, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Appear, and SceneLayer emit dedicated data-presentation hooks and forward authored classes.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit components provide structure and motion without a fallback visual theme.
evidence: The inspected kit renderers supply structural positioning, dimensions, and animation properties, but no fallback palette, typography, borders, or shadows. Arrow inherits currentColor.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation styling works with ordinary CSS and does not require a styling framework.
evidence: Talk imports its presentation-owned CSS and supplies className="htmap-talk". That stylesheet styles kit data hooks and authored entity classes using ordinary CSS rules.
package.json declares React, Motion, and icons as runtime dependencies, with no required CSS framework.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supports authored coordinates and dimensions without imposing a diagram layout system.
evidence: SceneLayer establishes an absolute inset layer. Box and Frame forward authored style props to motion.div.
Arrow animates supplied from/to coordinates into SVG line endpoints. MainScene uses explicit left, top, width, and height values for cards and overlays.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit itself renders and positions the default attribution link at bottom-right.
evidence: Presentation renders Attribution without requiring options. Attribution defaults to ATTRIBUTION_LABEL and ATTRIBUTION_HREF and applies position: fixed, right: 16, bottom: 16.
The constants supply 'made by and-scene' and https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene.

scene-kit.rationale: Attribution exposes a stable target for host-owned styling.
evidence: Attribution emits data-presentation-attribution and forwards options.className.

scene-kit.rationale: Header branding is absent by default and can be explicitly supplied by the host.
evidence: Presentation forwards brand to Header; Header renders the brand container only when brand is supplied.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative policy explicitly requires one-at-a-time questioning and asks only for missing information.
evidence: SKILL.md Procedure §1 specifies “one question at a time” and orders missing questions as topic, visual style, then step content and visual intent.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy explicitly permits building with partial detail when the user chooses to proceed.
evidence: Procedure §1 says to “build from what's captured instead of blocking on completeness” when the user chooses partial detail.

presentation-skill.rationale: Complete prompts explicitly bypass further requirements questions.
evidence: Procedure §1 says that when the prompt includes topic, style, and every step, “skip straight to building.”

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused executable test materializes the scaffold into a fresh empty directory, installs dependencies there, and checks its anchors and build.
evidence: INT-001 beforeAll creates tempDir with mkdtempSync, copies BOOTSTRAP_DIR into it, materializes a presentation, and runs npm ci with cwd: tempDir, rejecting a nonzero status.
The cases “provides all three contract anchors” and “builds the materialized app with no type or build errors” assert anchor files, build exit status zero, and dist/index.html.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy forbids rescaffolding existing anchors, but the required executable or workflow evidence for this branch is absent.
evidence: Procedure §3 says to use an existing anchored project without rescaffolding.
INT-001 starts with a fresh empty temporary directory and unconditionally copies the bootstrap; it never constructs an already-scaffolded target or asserts that its contents remain unchanged.

presentation-skill.rationale: Missing-anchor merging is described but lacks the required focused evidence.
evidence: The scaffolding reference requires preserving existing files and merging missing configuration.
INT-001 copies the entire bootstrap into an empty directory; it does not seed partial anchors, conflicting files, or existing dependency versions and assert their preservation.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap applies global visual defaults, directly contradicting its style-neutral requirement.
evidence: Bootstrap main.tsx imports index.css.
That stylesheet sets :root font-family, color #f8f3e6, background #0d0c0b, and line-height; body receives radial and linear gradient backgrounds.
The integration test only checks scene-kit stylesheet imports and Tailwind dependency names, which does not exclude these actual global defaults.

presentation-skill.rationale: The executable scaffold fixture resolves template sources independently of the caller's working directory and installs from the destination.
evidence: INT-001 derives REPO_ROOT from fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), then constructs SKILL_DIR and BOOTSTRAP_DIR using absolute joins.

beforeAll reads both bootstrap and presentation templates through those resolved paths and runs npm ci with cwd: tempDir; subsequent assertions check materialized anchors and a successful destination…

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused evidence exercises monorepo detection and installation into the resolved presentations/ app.
evidence: The scaffolding reference describes workspaces, pnpm-workspace.yaml, and packages/apps detection.
INT-001 creates none of those target states and copies directly into tempDir, so it cannot verify monorepo placement or preservation of the workspace root.

presentation-skill.rationale: The empty-directory fixture does not establish the distinct existing standalone-project branch required by the review guidance.
evidence: Procedure §3 selects the repository root for standalone projects.
INT-001 seeds no existing standalone project before copying the bootstrap and contains no assertions about resolving that project root or preserving its existing content.

presentation-skill.rationale: Confirmation is explicit policy, but no focused test or verified workflow exercises the nonempty-target confirmation branch.
evidence: Procedure §3 requires stating the resolved target and obtaining explicit confirmation before writes to a nonempty project missing anchors.
INT-001 performs unconditional copying into an empty directory; it supplies no confirmation choice and checks no pre-confirmation mutation boundary.

presentation-skill.rationale: The creation policy registers the new slug, and the delivered router and loader render its registered component.
evidence: Procedure §4 requires a new presentation folder and a registry entry containing slug, title, and a dynamic Talk import.
Bootstrap resolveRoute finds the registry entry matching the pathname slug; App.renderRoute passes it to getPresentationComponent, which caches lazy(entry.load), then renders it inside Suspense.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs presentation styling into its own stylesheet, and the template supports presentation-scoped styling through a root class.
evidence: Procedure §4 requires renaming the presentation CSS to its slug and writing the designed look there; the scope rules prohibit restyling the reusable kit for one presentation.
Template Talk imports ./__SLUG__.css and supplies className="__SLUG__-talk". Presentation applies that className to its root element, and PRESENTATION.css uses slug-specific selectors.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative creation and modification policies explicitly preserve other presentations and registry entries.
evidence: Procedure §4 Create requires adding one registry entry and says not to touch any other registry entry or presentation folder.
Procedure §4 Modify requires keeping every other presentation and the registry order untouched.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy requires resolving ambiguous modification targets before making changes.

### U6: The CI poller can't read this PR, and the repo has no CI
- The `codagent:wait-ci` poller (`check-ci.sh` in the harness plugin cache) requests the `gh pr view` field `baseRefOid`.
- The repository has no `.github/workflows`; git history shows it never had any. So there is no current-head CI run to poll, even with a working poller.

- Adding a GitHub Actions workflow would run on every eval branch and PR of this fixture repo. The approved test plan says INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001 and E2E-002 run "on every pull request", but no task delivered CI. That is a scope/cost decision.
1. Environment owner: upgrade `gh` in the eval image to a release that supports `baseRefOid`, or make `check-ci.sh` fall back when that field is unsupported.

2. Project owner: add a PR workflow (for example `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run verify`), or accept local-only verification for this fixture.
- *Upgrade gh or patch the script:* acceptance can collect CI evidence automatically. The change happens outside this repo.
- *Add CI:* matches the test plan's "every pull request" execution. Every run takes about 8+ minutes of browser-backed tests and uses Actions minutes on each eval branch.
- **AC-002 (U6):** reproduced unchanged. The poller still fails on `gh` 2.45.0's missing `baseRefOid`, and the repo still has no CI workflows. Still waiting on the U6 decisions:
- **Pre-test plan:** `exploration-plan.md` required the two prior finding reproductions, then zero-step sizing, then current-head CI.

- No `.github` workflow files or implementation CI checks are configured. The only status context is CodeRabbit `SUCCESS`; its informational comment says draft PRs are not reviewed, so this is not implementation validation. CI coverage is explicitly absent.

- The prescribed `check-ci.sh` remains unusable with the installed GitHub CLI because it requests unsupported `baseRefOid` (AC-002). The bundled comment fetcher succeeds and reports `has_comments: false`.
## AC-002 — CI poller cannot query this PR with installed GitHub CLI
- **Affected behavior:** Required current-head CI polling/handoff evidence.
- **Expected:** `codagent:wait-ci`'s bundled poller queries the current branch PR and returns checks/reviews for the tested SHA.

- **Observed:** `check-ci.sh` exits 1 with `{"error":"no PR found for current branch"}`. Running its exact `gh pr view --json number,url,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefOid,mergeable,mergeStateStatus` query directly shows the installed `gh` rejects `baseRefOid` as an unknown JSON field. PR #34 itself resolves by number, is open, mergeable, and points to the tested SHA. Its only status context is CodeRabbit `SUCCESS`, while its PR comment explicitly says the draft was not reviewed. No `.github` workflows are present. The bundled PR-comments script succeeds and finds no actionable comments.
- **Reproduction:** Run `bash /workspace/home/.codex/plugins/cache/codagent/codagent/0.12.0/skills/wait-ci/scripts/check-ci.sh` from the repository branch.

- **AC-002 reproduced:** `check-ci.sh` again returned `{"error":"no PR found for current branch"}`. Its exact `gh pr view --json ... baseRefOid ...` call again exited 1 with `Unknown JSON field: "baseRefOid"`. PR #34 remains open, mergeable, and head-matched; it has no configured CI workflows, and CodeRabbit explicitly skipped review because the PR is a draft. The bundled comment fetcher still finds no actionable comments.

- **AC-002 reproduced again:** `check-ci.sh` again returns `{"error":"no PR found for current branch"}`. The exact query exits 1 because the installed `gh` rejects `baseRefOid`. PR #34 is mergeable, open, draft, and head-matched; no implementation CI workflow/checks exist; CodeRabbit says the draft was not reviewed. The comment fetcher reports no actionable comments.

There is no tracked product change from the prior tested revision. Both outstanding findings reproduced: narrow diagram labels remain unreadable at 390×844 (AC-001), and the acceptance CI poller still fails because the installed GitHub CLI rejects its `baseRefOid` query (AC-002). **Status: NOT_READY.** AC-001 remains a product issue. AC-002 remains a workflow-tooling impediment. No broader testing was done because the diff is zero steps.
## CI

Automated CI is explicitly absent: there are no repository workflow files or implementation checks. GitHub reports only CodeRabbit `SUCCESS`, but its comment says the draft PR was not reviewed; that is not implementation validation. The current-head `check-ci.sh` failed because installed `gh` rejects `baseRefOid`; the bundled comments query found no actionable comments. PR #34 is mergeable and head-matched. No automated-validation CI evidence was supplied.
